description: Composite XRD figure made of two vertically stacked blocks, each holding four offset diffraction patterns. The x-axis is 2θ (°) spanning 40-100 with gridlines every 10°; the y-axis is Intensity (a.u.) with no numeric scale. The upper block is headed "Before tensile test" and the lower "After tensile test"; within each block four patterns are stacked from top to bottom and labelled, in the same order, olive QA-800, blue QA-740, teal QA-680 and red QA-620. Nine reflections are indexed at the top of the upper block — (111)γ, (110)α, (200)γ, (200)α, (220)γ, (211)α, (311)γ, (222)γ and (220)α — i.e. austenite (γ) and ferrite (α) reflections; the strongest pair of sharp peaks lies between the 40 and 46° 2θ gridlines. The lower block shows the same reflection set after deformation, with altered relative peak intensities. Although the supplied caption reads only "Table 4", the pixels show an XRD profile figure; the citing text indicates this is the XRD profile of Fig. 9(a), whose Rietveld refinement supplied the austenite stacking-fault-energy parameters listed in Table 4.

subfigures.description: Block headed "Before tensile test" containing four offset XRD patterns (2θ = 40-100°, Intensity a.u.) labelled top-to-bottom QA-800 (olive), QA-740 (blue), QA-680 (teal), QA-620 (red). Nine peak indices are printed above it: (111)γ, (110)α, (200)γ, (200)α, (220)γ, (211)α, (311)γ, (222)γ, (220)α. Strongest sharp peaks form a close pair between 40 and 46° 2θ.

Block headed "After tensile test" with the same four stacked, labelled patterns in the same order (QA-800, QA-740, QA-680, QA-620). No peak-index labels are printed in this block; the same γ/α reflections persist after deformation with changed relative peak intensities.

observations.observation: The figure plots X-ray diffraction patterns with x-axis 2θ (°) from 40 to 100 (gridlines every 10°) and y-axis Intensity (a.u.) with no numeric intensity scale.
The group is divided into an upper block headed "Before tensile test" and a lower block headed "After tensile test", each containing four offset patterns.
The four patterns in each block are labelled QA-800, QA-740, QA-680 and QA-620 from top to bottom (olive, blue, teal and red curves respectively).
Nine reflections are indexed in the upper block: (111)γ, (110)α, (200)γ, (200)α, (220)γ, (211)α, (311)γ, (222)γ and (220)α, covering austenite (γ) and ferrite (α) phases.
The strongest peaks in every pattern form a sharp close pair located between the 40 and 46 ° 2θ gridlines, at the (111)γ and (110)α positions.
The lower block contains the same reflection set after tensile testing, with relative peak intensities differing from the corresponding curves in the upper block.
No numeric intensity values or exact 2θ peak positions are printed anywhere on the figure.
The supplied caption is only "Table 4", which does not describe the diffraction patterns actually rendered in the pixels.
The citing text states the SFE parameters were obtained by Rietveld refinement analysis for XRD profiles (Fig. 9(a)) or gained from reference [51].
The citing text states that the SFEs of QA specimens were between 20 mJ/m² and 40 mJ/m², implying a TWIP effect in austenite during deformation.

The citing text states the SFEs of QA specimens changed with annealing temperature, being reduced for QA-620 relative to QA-680 by carbide precipitation and lower annealing temperature, and decreasing above 680 °C with increasing temperature due to elemental partitioning.

The figure supplies the XRD profiles used to obtain the Zener elastic anisotropy, <111> shear modulus, lattice constant aO, root-mean-square microstrain ε_SO² over 50 Å, and stacking fault probability used for the SFE calculation.
